title: Israel's Disobedience and the Cycle of Judges

date.label: Undated Judges narrative
date.note: Biblical narrative chronology is not independently established as an absolute BCE date.

claims.claim: Judges 2:11–23 explicitly articulates an idealized judge-deliverance recurrence
claims.evidence: Judges 2:11–23 (Hebrew Bible, Judges 1–21, Masoretic text, read in full in Hebrew and JPS English via Mechon Mamre). Textual description only; the narrated event is not externally corroborated.
Judges 2:6–10 (Hebrew Bible, Judges 1–21, Masoretic text, read in full in Hebrew and JPS English via Mechon Mamre). Textual description only; the narrated event is not externally corroborated.

connections.note: Parallel dismissal, death and generation transition: Joshua 24:28–31 and Judges 2:6–10 both report Joshua's dismissal of the people, his death, and the passing of the generation that knew the LORD's works. What they share is a literary relationship between texts; agreement among biblical passages is not equivalent to independent confirmation of the episodes.
Intermarriage and other-god prohibitions (Deuteronomy 7:1–6). This is a literary/thematic relation, not an independently verified shared historical event.
Retrospective covenant failure and distress motif (Psalm 106:34–46). This is a literary/thematic relation, not an independently verified shared historical event.
